note: getProcessor returns the test field `processor`, which is a lambda (unrepresentable in the record) in every recorded call: each of the 12 recorded test methods makes exactly one testSame, from createBuilderIncludingCode, right after assigning `processor` (and resetting labelToId and the local testTypes map). The holder replays that assignment (prepareProcessor) and then the verbatim getProcessor body. A fresh holder per getProcessor call is equivalent to the test instance because getNumRepetitions is 1 in every record, JUnit creates a new test instance per method, and the only state the lambda reads besides the AST is the graphNodeFactory, which the test also creates once per instance. The graph built afterwards from testTypes/labelToId and the test's assertions on it are not replayed; the side output they read (labelToId, the graphNodeFactory's nodes, and testTypes inside the processor lambda's captures) is compared post-call through testFieldsAfter (classify round 1, batch 9). createCompiler returns the test's `compiler` field, a plain `new Compiler()` built at construction (harness.effective.createCompiler is Compiler), so the replay's CompilerTestCase.createCompiler() is used instead: it differs only by setAllowableFeatures(acceptedLanguage) (overwritten by Compiler.initOptions from the same options.languageIn), setPreferRegexParser(false) (the Compiler default) and an empty webpackModulesById. The one unreproduced effect is that the test's createCompiler returns the same instance on every call, so the harness's expected-output parse (parseExpectedJs, after the processing and warning checks) re-initialises the compiler that produced the result, while the replay parses the expected output on a fresh compiler; the recorded observed errors and warnings are empty in all 12 records and the recorded outcome is normal, so nothing observable depends on it. setUp's enableTypeCheck/replaceTypesWithColors/disableCompareJsDoc are restored from harness.fields.
